pairs.subject: background-jobs
pairs.evidence: src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts:15 cancelWorkflowJob resolves void while the backend writes terminal Failed at once (src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684) and WorkflowJob omits cancel_outcome (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workflows.rs:18), so no client can show cancelling or tell cancelled from failed

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/background_job.rs:684 cancel() sets JobStatus::Failed immediately (no cancelling state, no distinct cancelled terminal); src/lib/bindings/WorkflowJob.ts:3 status is an open string with no progress/phase field, only elapsed_secs and line_count
src/api/pipeline/workflows.ts:9 getWorkflowsOverview is a cold snapshot with a bounded output_tail per job, keyed by job_id (workflows.ts:12)
src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:22 getSubscriptionHealth exposes per-loop alive, lastTickAt, errorCount and consecutivePanics, so a silent loop is detectable from the client

pairs.registryProposal: Re-judge of the 2026-10-10 verdict against the same digest/revision: unchanged code, deviation holds. loop-supervision, tick-isolation, adaptive-cadence and startup-sweeps are realized (or not) in src-tauri backend contexts, not in this TS IPC-wrapper context; the subject would be better paired with the backend scheduler/background_job context than with api-pipeline, where only the job contract and health surface are visible.
